newsitem.title: USA: White House to propose DC aid package on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: White House to propose DC aid package on Thursday.

text.p: The White House plans to propose a major aid package for the District of Columbia on Thursday, including having the U.S. government pay 70 percent of the city's Medicaid bills instead of the current 50 percent, a source familiar with the plan said on Monday.

In addition, the federal government would assume full payment of a massive unfunded pension liability for city firefighters, police, teachers and judges the District inherited from the U.S. when it won Home Rule in 1974, the source told Reuters.
The liability reached about $1.8 billion around 1980 and is now close to $4.4 billion, the source said.

Andrew Brimmer, chairman of the city's congressionally mandated financial control board, recently warned that the city's pension problem will reach "catastrophic" proportions early in the next century.

The White House also will recommend that the U.S. take responsibility for incarceration of the city's roughly 7,000 felony prisoners, the source said. It is unclear if prisoners would be transferred to jails in other states or remain in local facilities, the source said.

In return for the aid, the District would forfeit an annual $660 million payment it currently gets from Congress to offset what it loses from tax-exempt federal properties, under the White House plan, the source said.
On the other hand, the White House also will propose a package of tax incentives aimed at encouraging business and jobs in the financially troubled city, the source said.
